captions.text: In Inventory, open Issuances and find the item that has come back.
This example follows Academy training batteries after an earlier partial return.
The row still shows one outstanding, the Personnel
location, and Partially returned.
Check the item, outstanding quantity and expected return date together.
Select Return on that row to open its return form.
This is a fictional software exercise in the training department.

scenes.title: Read the return form before entering changes

captions.text: The Return dialog separates Amount, Destination location, Status and Note.
Amount starts at the remaining quantity.
The destination is initially blank, and the status is In service.
The help beneath Destination location says to leave it blank
when consuming or writing stock off.
For this exercise the item is being returned to a stock location, so we will
select a destination before submitting.
Close exits this dialog without making the prepared return.

scenes.title: Choose where the returned stock goes

captions.text: Set Amount to one and choose Station as the Destination location.
Leave Status at In service for the intended return.
Add a clear note explaining the movement.
Here it says that the remaining fictional training battery pack is
going back to Station, and that no physical movement is taking place.
The quantity and destination are separate decisions: one tells Resgrid
how much came back, and the other tells it where that stock is going.
The Status control also offers Out for repair and Damaged.
These screens show those choices selected in the form before saving.
The help describes Status as the state the equipment came back in.
Choose the condition that matches the actual return, following
your department procedure.
In this recording we inspect both alternatives and then restore In service;
we do not post a damaged or repair return.

scenes.title: Submit the final return and verify its result

captions.text: Before submitting, check the final form again: one item, Station, In
service, and the training note.
Select Return at the bottom of the dialog.
The returned Issuances table now shows zero outstanding and a green
Returned status on the same item row.
Its Return action is gone.
This saved result is the check that the last outstanding quantity has been
cleared; a completed form alone would not establish that the return was stored.
Open History to inspect the movement ledger.
Filter to Academy training batteries.
The newest row is a Return of one, moving from Personnel to Station,
with the same explanatory note.
The earlier partial return and the earlier Consume row remain
visible as separate movements.
Check the quantity, direction and note together when explaining a balance change.
This review uses the ledger as shown; no witness attestation or
stock-balance rebuild is performed.
Return to On hand and apply the item filter.
Before this return, the recorded balances were thirteen at Station,
five at Unit and one at Personnel.
After the return, they are fourteen at Station, five at
Unit and zero at Personnel.
The total stays nineteen.
Returning issued stock changes where that quantity is held; it does not reverse
the separate earlier consumption or restore the original receipt of twenty.

scenes.title: Use the same review across department types

captions.text: Use the same quantity, location and condition checks for
other department equipment.
A search-and-rescue team can track returned radio batteries, a
security company can track issued equipment, and a wildland contractor
can reconcile field supplies.
Community paramedicine and mental health response teams, industrial emergency
teams, and fire and E M S departments can use the same recorded return process.
Agree who records returns, and verify both the issuance and the location
balances after each exercise.
